To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the shear viscosity of hadrons can be significantly reduced by hadron interactions that lead to the formation of resonances, and that the shear viscosity to entropy density ratio \eta/s of a hadronic gas approaches that of the QGP at the QCD phase boundary temperature Tc.
hadron resonances increase entropy density and decrease shear viscosity, leading to a substantial decrease in the ratio \eta/s.

the inclusion of resonances in the hadronic gas reduces the shear viscosity and increases the entropy density leading, as expected, to a substantial reduction in the ratio \eta/s as we approach the phase transition temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the shear viscosity of hadrons and its relation to entropy density, as well as the effect of the QCD phase change on these properties.
the study of transport properties of hadrons and their relevance to the QCD phase diagram.
the study of the shear viscosity of a hadronic gas of interacting pions, kaons, nucleons and eta-mesons using different hadronic cross section models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hadronic interactions forming resonant structures are important for the transport coefficients.

the shear viscosity to entropy density ratio of a hadronic gas is smaller than the value of 1/4 \pi which is obtained from the ideal Boltzmann limit and the lower bound of 1/2 \pi which is the value for a free massless Boltzmann gas.
the K-matrix cross section parametrization leads to a lower value of \eta/s than the BW parametrization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shear viscosity to entropy density ratio is significantly reduced by the inclusion of resonances in the hadronic medium.
the K-matrix cross section parametrization of resonances leads to the smallest \eta/s of the hadronic gas.
the K-matrix approach is the most reliable method to calculate hadronic cross sections and the resulting transport coefficients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shear viscosity of hadrons is significantly reduced when hadronic interactions form resonances.
the K-matrix approach provides a more accurate description of hadronic interactions and thus should be used in transport calculations.
hadron resonance gas with K-matrix interactions is an excellent approximation to the shear viscosity of a hadronic gas at temperatures below the phase transition temperature.
